# Indiana dig-damage enforcement desk (no-code edition)

You answer actuarial questions about Indiana's dig-damage enforcement record: the Indiana Utility Regulatory
Commission's orders approving the Underground Plant Protection Advisory Committee's recommendations under IC 8-1-26.
The data is 9,958 recommendation forms ("cases") from 58 orders dated 2021-01-01 to 2025-12-31.

## What you can and cannot do

You have Read, Grep and Glob only. You cannot run code, open the raw case table (it is not in this folder), or use a calculator
beyond your own arithmetic. So you answer from **pre-computed tables** in `reference/tables/`. Those tables hold counts, dollar sums,
means, medians, percentiles, histograms, name counts and top-N lists, cut by order year, base section, qualifier, respondent type and
outcome. You may combine table rows by hand: add counts and sums, take differences, ratios and shares. You may NOT invent a cut
that no table supports. When a question needs one, say so plainly and give the closest figure, labelled (see `rules.md`, section 4).

## Read order

| Step | Read | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | this README | orientation |
| 2 | `rules.md` | how to answer, the traps, how to combine rows |
| 3 | `examples.md` | the answer shape, worked from real table rows |
| 4 | `reference/tables/INDEX.md` | which table answers which kind of question, and the legend of codes |
| 5 | the one or two tables you need | Grep a table id, for example `Grep "### S7" -A 40`, rather than reading a whole file |
| 6 | `identity.md` only if unsure the question is in scope; `reference/glossary.md` for what a section or qualifier means; `reference/SCHEMA.md` for a column or known defect (Grep it, do not read it whole) |

## What is where

    README.md  identity.md  rules.md  examples.md
    reference/tables/INDEX.md          start here for numbers
    reference/tables/01_overview_time.md    totals, years, orders, quarters, damage years, lags
    reference/tables/02_cube.md             year x base section x qualifier x respondent type: counts, dollars, outcome mix
    reference/tables/03_penalty_stats.md    mean, median, percentiles, outcome mix, recommendation wording
    reference/tables/04_histograms.md       counts at each dollar value for many segments
    reference/tables/05_respondents_repeat.md   repeat names, rank, concentration, named lists
    reference/tables/06_utility_types_otherparty.md   utility companies, respondent kinds, other party
    reference/tables/07_places_committee_notes.md     cities, abstentions, notes, scan pages
    reference/glossary.md              what the sections and qualifiers mean, with an evidence tag on each statement
    reference/SCHEMA.md                the data dictionary and known defects

## If a question asks about X, go to Y

| The question asks about | Go to |
|---|---|
| a count, share or trend by order year, section, qualifier, utility or not | cube (02) or tables A, B, C (01) |
| mean, median, spread, total of penalties | 03 (S tables); the cube for sums |
| how many cases at or above $X; a percentile for an unusual cut | 04 histograms |
| repeat offenders, "the same respondent again", concentration | 05 |
| a utility company by name (CenterPoint, NIPSCO ...) | 06 U tables, and 05 T6 |
| what a section or qualifier is | `reference/glossary.md` |
| company size, digs or tickets, exposure, who excavated, fines paid, claim cost | not in the data: say so (`rules.md`, section 6) |

The question's own definitions always win over this folder. If a question defines a term differently from the preamble or from
`rules.md`, follow the question and say so in one line. If the question's definition cannot be met from the tables, say which
table gets closest.

1	# SCHEMA: what the case table holds (data dictionary)
2	
3	The pre-computed tables in `tables/` were built from a 14-column case table (cleaned: 24 known cell errors already fixed). You
4	cannot open that table; this page tells you what each column means and where the data is unreliable, so you can judge a table's figure.
5	Counts below are for the raw parse unless a line says the cleaned table differs. "Page image" means the page rendered from the original
6	PDF and looked at.
7	
8	## What a case is
9	
10	One row is one **recommendation form page**: one page of an order PDF that carries the Indiana Underground Plant Protection Advisory Committee "Recommendation to IURC" form. There are 9,958 rows from 58 order PDFs. The cover page and any other page of an order are not rows. Five blank copies of the form are were dropped and are not in the data.
11	
12	A row is not one unique case number. 23 case numbers appear in more than one order (46 rows). Two `(order_file, case_number)` pairs appear on two pages of the same order each (4 rows); see `case_number`. The key that is always unique is `(order_file, page)`.
13	
14	## What is NOT in the data
15	
16	- Company size (of either party).
17	- The number of digs or tickets behind a case.
18	- The trade or kind of work of the respondent (the data has a name only).
19	- Whether a recommended penalty was paid, trained out, appealed or changed later.
20	- Which party is the utility and which is the excavator. Either name can appear in either of `respondent` and `other_party`.
21	- Anything from the cover page or other non-form pages of an order.
22	
23	## The violation qualifiers seen
24	
25	A qualifier is a word in parentheses printed after a cite, for example `IC 8-1-26-16(h)(expire)`. Letter or number marks such as `(h)`, `(a)(2)` and `(3)(b)` are part of the section and are not qualifiers. 1,902 cites carry a qualifier. Seven different qualifiers occur:
26	
27	| qualifier | cites |
28	|---|---|
29	| (locator-error) | 600 |
30	| (expire) | 518 |
31	| (prior) | 272 |
32	| (records) | 249 |
33	| (out) | 191 |
34	| (no-response) | 52 |
35	| (other) | 20 |
36	
37	This page does not say what the qualifiers or cites mean in law. That belongs in the questions step.
38	
39	## Columns
40	
41	### order_file
42	- **Meaning:** the order PDF the page is in.
43	- **On the page:** not on the page. It is the file name of the PDF.
44	- **Type and format:** string, matches `ord_PSD_MMDDYY.pdf` (also `ord_PSD_MM.DD.YY.pdf` for one file and `ord_PSDNPT_MMDDYY.pdf` for one file).
45	- **Allowed:** the 58 file names. Never blank.
46	- **Known defects:** none.
47	- **Treat as:** an identifier. `ord_PSDNPT_040622.pdf` (1 row) and `ord_PSD_040622.pdf` are two files with the same order date.
48	
49	### order_date
50	- **Meaning:** the date of the order the page is in.
51	- **On the page:** not on the page. It is read from the file name.
52	- **Type and format:** date, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. Never blank.
53	- **Allowed:** 57 distinct values, 2021-02-03 to 2025-12-10.
54	- **Known defects:** none seen. The date is only as right as the file name.
55	- **Treat as:** the order date, not the date of the damage or of the committee meeting.
56	
57	### page
58	- **Meaning:** the page of the order PDF the form is on. The cover page is page 1.
59	- **On the page:** not printed. It is the position in the PDF.
60	- **Type and format:** int, 2 to 346.
61	- **Allowed:** a positive whole number. Never blank.
62	- **Known defects:** none.
63	- **Treat as:** with `order_file`, the unique key of a row. Use it to find the page for a check.
64	
65	### case_number
66	- **Meaning:** the case number printed on the form.
67	- **On the page:** `Case Number:`
68	- **Type and format:** string of 5 digits.
69	- **Allowed:** `\d{5}`. Never blank in the data.
70	- **Known defects:**
71	  - 1 row holds `0` (ord_PSD_020321.pdf page 27). Its text layer reads `Case Number: 0`, `Respondent: 130 2nd St NE`, `Damage Location: Internattional Inc., Indianapolis` and a recommendation of `.5000`. The form looks filled in with values in the wrong boxes. Not corrected: the case number is not known from the page text, and the page image was not part of the ledger job. Treat the row as unusable for case-level counts.
72	  - 2 duplicate `(order_file, case_number)` pairs, 4 rows. Both were checked on the page image (ledger job):
73	    - ord_PSD_051822.pdf pages 7 and 346, case 25064: two real forms with the same parties, dates and location and a different cite (`IC 8-1-26-16(h)` and `IC 8-1-26-20(a)(2)`), both with a recommendation of `$10,000`. Abstentions read `Smith` and `Rick Smith`. Kept as two rows.
74	    - ord_PSD_101525.pdf pages 245 and 246, case 33669: two pages that are identical on the image. Kept as two rows; a reader who counts cases should count them once.
75	- **Treat as:** an identifier, not a number. Do not count distinct values as distinct cases without reading the duplicate note above.
76	
77	### respondent
78	- **Meaning:** the first named party of the form.
79	- **On the page:** `Respondent:`
80	- **Type and format:** string, free text, as printed.
81	- **Allowed:** any text. Blank in 1 row.
82	- **Known defects:**
83	  - 2 rows hold form text from the neighbouring label: `Date nf Advisory Meeting: One House At A Time` (ord_PSD_110321.pdf page 124) and `Date of Dam.age: Dam.age Location: Wickey Construction` (page 168). Both are scan pages. Not corrected (outside the ledger job).
84	  - Spelling variants of one company are not merged. `Internattional Inc.` appears in 16 rows in this column and 7 in `other_party`. Spelling on the page was not checked.
85	  - 62 rows have the same text in `respondent` and `other_party`.
86	- **Treat as:** a name for display, not a join key. Clean it before grouping companies.
87	
88	### other_party
89	- **Meaning:** the second named party of the form.
90	- **On the page:** `Other Party:`
91	- **Type and format:** string, free text, as printed.
92	- **Allowed:** any text. Blank in 27 rows.
93	- **Known defects:** 1 row holds the violation heading text (ord_PSD_110321.pdf page 106, a scan page), and its `respondent` holds both names and an address. Not corrected (outside the ledger job).
94	- **Treat as:** as `respondent`. Blank means nothing was printed or parsed.
95	
96	### advisory_meeting_date
97	- **Meaning:** the date of the advisory meeting.
98	- **On the page:** `Date of Advisory Meeting:`
99	- **Type and format:** date as printed, month/day/year with no leading zero in all but one row, for example `3/17/2022`.
100	- **Allowed:** `\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{4}`, 2019-01-15 to 2025-10-15. 63 distinct values. Blank in 1 row.
101	- **Known defects:** 1 row holds `12:00:00 AM` (ord_PSD_020321.pdf page 27, the case `0` row above). 1 row is blank (ord_PSD_022322.pdf page 129, a form with almost nothing filled in; page image checked, the field is empty on the page).
102	- **Treat as:** a text date. Parse it with `%m/%d/%Y` and treat the two defects as missing.
103	
104	### damage_date
105	- **Meaning:** the date the damage happened.
106	- **On the page:** `Date of Damage:`
107	- **Type and format:** date as printed, month/day/year, for example `6/9/2021`.
108	- **Allowed:** `\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{4}`, 2018-03-17 to 2025-08-22. By year: 2018 4, 2019 36, 2020 1,630, 2021 1,858, 2022 2,015, 2023 1,970, 2024 1,813, 2025 631. Blank in 1 row.
109	- **Known defects:** the one blank row is the same ord_PSD_022322.pdf page 129 (empty on the page image).
110	- **Treat as:** the damage date. The 40 rows before 2020 are real dates on the page (8 of them are the checkbox-form pages of ord_PSD_042121.pdf, checked on image).
111	
112	### damage_location
113	- **Meaning:** the street address and city of the damage.
114	- **On the page:** `Damage Location:`
115	- **Type and format:** string, `street, city`.
116	- **Allowed:** any text with a comma followed by a city. Blank in 9 rows.
117	- **Known defects:** 4 rows have no city: `3846 Schneider Street` (ord_PSD_101525.pdf pages 245 and 246, no city printed on the page image), `7401 ##` (ord_PSD_100924.pdf page 37) and `IC 8-1-26-16(h)` (ord_PSD_110321.pdf page 106, a scan page). The two last values were not corrected (outside the ledger job).
118	- **Treat as:** free text. The city is the text after the last comma when there is one. Spelling and abbreviation vary.
119	
120	### violations
121	- **Meaning:** the cite(s) the Pipeline Safety Division found, as printed.
122	- **On the page:** the line after `The IURC Pipeline Safety Division finds the following violation(s):`
123	- **Type and format:** string, one or more cites joined by `; `. Every row has exactly one cite or none; no row has two.
124	- **Allowed:** `IC 8-1-26-<section>` with a section of `16(h)`, `16(i)`, `18(h)`, `18(j)`, `19(c)`, `20(a)(1)`, `20(a)(2)`, `20(a)(3)(a)` or `20(a)(3)(b)`, optionally followed by one of the seven qualifiers above. Blank in 1 row.
125	- **Known defects:**
126	  - 16 rows have a cite the OCR misread (all scan pages), for example `IC 8-1-26-lS(h)`, `IC 8-l-26-16(h)`, `IC 8-1-26-20(a)(l)`, `IC8-l-26-16(h)` and `IC 8-1-26-16(b)` (two rows, page image shows `16(h)`). Ledger.
127	  - 1 row is blank (ord_PSD_022322.pdf page 129): the page image shows the violation line empty on the page. Not a parse error; left blank.
128	  - Scan rows whose cite is a valid-looking string were not each checked against the page image; only strings that failed the pattern or were rare were.
129	- **Treat as:** a code string. Split the base section from the qualifier before grouping, and keep rows with no qualifier separate from rows with one.
130	
131	### recommendation
132	- **Meaning:** the penalty the committee recommended, as printed.
133	- **On the page:** the text after `The Advisory Committee recommends the following penalty:` (or `civil penalty:`) up to `Abstentions:`.
134	- **Type and format:** string, free text. 133 distinct raw values. Wording varies for the same outcome (`Warning letter` 1,386 rows and `Warning Letter` 135 rows; `$1,500, respondent can complete training instead of paying $1,500` and longer versions with extra text).
135	- **Allowed:** any text. Blank in 2 rows (ord_PSD_022322.pdf page 196 and ord_PSD_110321.pdf page 168; neither was looked at on the page image).
136	- **Known defects:**
137	  - 8 rows are the checkbox form (ord_PSD_042121.pdf pages 149 to 156): the text layer holds every option with its box glyph, not the ticked option. Ledger: the ticked option from the page image, worded as printed on the form. Seven are `Training or $5,000 civil penalty if fail to complete training` (this form wording differs from the typed-form wording `Training or $5,000 if respondent fails to complete training` used elsewhere); one is `Civil penalty of $1,500; can mitigate $1,500 by completing training`.
138	  - 7 rows read `$$1000` (ord_PSD_060822.pdf pages 85 to 88 and 90 to 92). Page image checked: the doubled dollar sign and the missing comma are printed on the page. Not corrected.
139	  - 1 row reads `$3, 500; no ticket escalation - additional $1,000 ($4,500)` (ord_PSD_122821.pdf page 4). Page image checked: the space after the comma is printed on the page. A parser that reads the first amount gets 3. Not corrected.
140	  - 3 rows have an amount without a dollar sign: `.5000` (the case `0` row), `3000` (ord_PSD_060822.pdf page 290) and `0` (ord_PSD_080322.pdf page 222). Not corrected (outside the ledger job).
141	- **Treat as:** text to classify, not a number. Read dollar amounts with a rule that tolerates the printed oddities above, and handle the checkbox pages from the corrected value.
142	
143	### abstentions
144	- **Meaning:** the surname(s) printed after `Abstentions:`, one per member who abstained.
145	- **On the page:** `Abstentions:`
146	- **Type and format:** string, free text.
147	- **Allowed:** any text. Blank in 5,035 rows (nothing printed). 15 distinct values; `Smith` 3,824 and `Warren` 1,033 are the most common.
148	- **Known defects:** 2 rows carry the next label's text, `Smith Additional Infonnation:` and `Additional Infonnation:` (ord_PSD_110321.pdf pages 20 and 53, scan pages). Not corrected (outside the ledger job).
149	- **Treat as:** names as printed. `Rick Smith`, `Smith & Sontag` and similar variants exist.
150	
151	### additional_info
152	- **Meaning:** the free-text note after `Additional Information:`.
153	- **On the page:** `Additional Information:`
154	- **Type and format:** string, free text.
155	- **Allowed:** any text. Blank in 9,803 rows; 155 rows have a note.
156	- **Known defects:** none counted.
157	- **Treat as:** a note. Do not assume a blank means anything about the case.
158	
159	### scan
160	- **Meaning:** whether the page is a scanned image rather than typed text.
161	- **On the page:** not printed. It is derived from the PDF.
162	- **Type and format:** enum.
163	- **Allowed:** `yes` or `no`. `yes` in 182 rows, `no` in 9,776. Never blank.
164	- **Known defects:** none. 173 of the `yes` rows are in ord_PSD_110321.pdf, 8 in ord_PSD_042121.pdf (the checkbox pages) and 1 in ord_PSDNPT_040622.pdf.
165	- **Treat as:** a warning flag. Scan pages were read from OCR text, so most of the OCR errors and the label-first layout errors above are on scan pages.
166	
167	## Corrections already applied
168	
169	24 cells were corrected after the parse, each checked on the page image: 8 `recommendation` cells (the checkbox-form pages of
170	ord_PSD_042121.pdf, pages 149 to 156) and 16 `violations` cells (OCR errors in the cite). The tables use the corrected values.
171	
172	Looked at on the page image and left as they are:
173	
174	- 7 `$$1000` rows and the `$3, 500` row: printed that way on the page (the PREAMBLE rule reads them as $1,000 and $3,500).
175	- The two duplicate `(order_file, case_number)` pairs: two real forms (case 25064) and one identical repeated page (case 33669).
176	- The blank `violations` row (ord_PSD_022322.pdf page 129): the violation line is empty on the page, as are `other_party`, both dates and the city of the location.

Its text layer reads `Case Number: 0`, `Respondent: 130 2nd St NE`, `Damage Location: Internattional Inc., Indianapolis` and a recommendation of `.5000`. The form looks filled in with values in the wrong boxes. Not corrected: the case number is not known from the page text, and the page image was not part of the ledger job. Treat the row as unusable for case-level counts.
  - 2 duplicate `(order_file, case_number)` pairs, 4 rows. Both were checked on the page image (ledger job):
    - ord_PSD_051822.pdf pages 7 and 346, case 25064: two real forms with the same parties, dates and location and a different cite (`IC 8-1-26-16(h)` and `IC 8-1-26-20(a)(2)`), both with a recommendation of `$10,000`. Abstentions read `Smith` and `Rick Smith`. Kept as two rows.
    - ord_PSD_101525.pdf pages 245 and 246, case 33669: two pages that are identical on the image. Kept as two rows; a reader who counts cases should count them once.
- **Treat as:** an identifier, not a number. Do not count distinct values as distinct cases without reading the duplicate note above.

### respondent
- **Meaning:** the first named party of the form.
- **On the page:** `Respondent:`
- **Type and format:** string, free text, as printed.
- **Allowed:** any text. Blank in 1 row.
- **Known defects:**
  - 2 rows hold form text from the neighbouring label: `Date nf Advisory Meeting: One House At A Time` (ord_PSD_110321.pdf page 124) and `Date of Dam.age: Dam.age Location: Wickey Construction` (page 168). Both are scan pages. Not corrected (outside the ledger job).
  - Spelling variants of one company are not merged. `Internattional Inc.` appears in 16 rows in this column and 7 in `other_party`. Spelling on the page was not checked.
  - 62 rows have the same text in `respondent` and `other_party`.
- **Treat as:** a name for display, not a join key. Clean it before grouping companies.

### other_party
- **Meaning:** the second named party of the form.
- **On the page:** `Other Party:`
- **Type and format:** string, free text, as printed.
- **Allowed:** any text. Blank in 27 rows.
- **Known defects:** 1 row holds the violation heading text (ord_PSD_110321.pdf page 106, a scan page), and its `respondent` holds both names and an address. Not corrected (outside the ledger job).
- **Treat as:** as `respondent`. Blank means nothing was printed or parsed.

### advisory_meeting_date
- **Meaning:** the date of the advisory meeting.
- **On the page:** `Date of Advisory Meeting:`
- **Type and format:** date as printed, month/day/year with no leading zero in all but one row, for example `3/17/2022`.
- **Allowed:** `\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{4}`, 2019-01-15 to 2025-10-15. 63 distinct values. Blank in 1 row.
- **Known defects:** 1 row holds `12:00:00 AM` (ord_PSD_020321.pdf page 27, the case `0` row above). 1 row is blank (ord_PSD_022322.pdf page 129, a form with almost nothing filled in; page image checked, the field is empty on the page).
- **Treat as:** a text date. Parse it with `%m/%d/%Y` and treat the two defects as missing.

### damage_date
- **Meaning:** the date the damage happened.
- **On the page:** `Date of Damage:`
- **Type and format:** date as printed, month/day/year, for example `6/9/2021`.
- **Allowed:** `\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{4}`, 2018-03-17 to 2025-08-22. By year: 2018 4, 2019 36, 2020 1,630, 2021 1,858, 2022 2,015, 2023 1,970, 2024 1,813, 2025 631. Blank in 1 row.
- **Known defects:** the one blank row is the same ord_PSD_022322.pdf page 129 (empty on the page image).
- **Treat as:** the damage date. The 40 rows before 2020 are real dates on the page (8 of them are the checkbox-form pages of ord_PSD_042121.pdf, checked on image).

### damage_location
- **Meaning:** the street address and city of the damage.
- **On the page:** `Damage Location:`
- **Type and format:** string, `street, city`.
- **Allowed:** any text with a comma followed by a city. Blank in 9 rows.
- **Known defects:** 4 rows have no city: `3846 Schneider Street` (ord_PSD_101525.pdf pages 245 and 246, no city printed on the page image), `7401 ##` (ord_PSD_100924.pdf page 37) and `IC 8-1-26-16(h)` (ord_PSD_110321.pdf page 106, a scan page). The two last values were not corrected (outside the ledger job).
- **Treat as:** free text. The city is the text after the last comma when there is one. Spelling and abbreviation vary.

### violations
- **Meaning:** the cite(s) the Pipeline Safety Division found, as printed.
- **On the page:** the line after `The IURC Pipeline Safety Division finds the following violation(s):`
- **Type and format:** string, one or more cites joined by `; `. Every row has exactly one cite or none; no row has two.
- **Allowed:** `IC 8-1-26-<section>` with a section of `16(h)`, `16(i)`, `18(h)`, `18(j)`, `19(c)`, `20(a)(1)`, `20(a)(2)`, `20(a)(3)(a)` or `20(a)(3)(b)`, optionally followed by one of the seven qualifiers above. Blank in 1 row.
- **Known defects:**
  - 16 rows have a cite the OCR misread (all scan pages), for example `IC 8-1-26-lS(h)`, `IC 8-l-26-16(h)`, `IC 8-1-26-20(a)(l)`, `IC8-l-26-16(h)` and `IC 8-1-26-16(b)` (two rows, page image shows `16(h)`). Ledger.
  - 1 row is blank (ord_PSD_022322.pdf page 129): the page image shows the violation line empty on the page. Not a parse error; left blank.
  - Scan rows whose cite is a valid-looking string were not each checked against the page image; only strings that failed the pattern or were rare were.
- **Treat as:** a code string. Split the base section from the qualifier before grouping, and keep rows with no qualifier separate from rows with one.

### recommendation
- **Meaning:** the penalty the committee recommended, as printed.
- **On the page:** the text after `The Advisory Committee recommends the following penalty:` (or `civil penalty:`) up to `Abstentions:`.
- **Type and format:** string, free text. 133 distinct raw values. Wording varies for the same outcome (`Warning letter` 1,386 rows and `Warning Letter` 135 rows; `$1,500, respondent can complete training instead of paying $1,500` and longer versions with extra text).
- **Allowed:** any text. Blank in 2 rows (ord_PSD_022322.pdf page 196 and ord_PSD_110321.pdf page 168; neither was looked at on the page image).
- **Known defects:**
  - 8 rows are the checkbox form (ord_PSD_042121.pdf pages 149 to 156): the text layer holds every option with its box glyph, not the ticked option. Ledger: the ticked option from the page image, worded as printed on the form. Seven are `Training or $5,000 civil penalty if fail to complete training` (this form wording differs from the typed-form wording `Training or $5,000 if respondent fails to complete training` used elsewhere); one is `Civil penalty of $1,500; can mitigate $1,500 by completing training`.
  - 7 rows read `$$1000` (ord_PSD_060822.pdf pages 85 to 88 and 90 to 92). Page image checked: the doubled dollar sign and the missing comma are printed on the page. Not corrected.
  - 1 row reads `$3, 500; no ticket escalation - additional $1,000 ($4,500)` (ord_PSD_122821.pdf page 4). Page image checked: the space after the comma is printed on the page. A parser that reads the first amount gets 3. Not corrected.
  - 3 rows have an amount without a dollar sign: `.5000` (the case `0` row), `3000` (ord_PSD_060822.pdf page 290) and `0` (ord_PSD_080322.pdf page 222). Not corrected (outside the ledger job).
- **Treat as:** text to classify, not a number. Read dollar amounts with a rule that tolerates the printed oddities above, and handle the checkbox pages from the corrected value.

### abstentions
- **Meaning:** the surname(s) printed after `Abstentions:`, one per member who abstained.
- **On the page:** `Abstentions:`
- **Type and format:** string, free text.
- **Allowed:** any text. Blank in 5,035 rows (nothing printed). 15 distinct values; `Smith` 3,824 and `Warren` 1,033 are the most common.
- **Known defects:** 2 rows carry the next label's text, `Smith Additional Infonnation:` and `Additional Infonnation:` (ord_PSD_110321.pdf pages 20 and 53, scan pages). Not corrected (outside the ledger job).
- **Treat as:** names as printed. `Rick Smith`, `Smith & Sontag` and similar variants exist.

### additional_info
- **Meaning:** the free-text note after `Additional Information:`.
- **On the page:** `Additional Information:`
- **Type and format:** string, free text.
- **Allowed:** any text. Blank in 9,803 rows; 155 rows have a note.
- **Known defects:** none counted.
- **Treat as:** a note. Do not assume a blank means anything about the case.

### scan
- **Meaning:** whether the page is a scanned image rather than typed text.
- **On the page:** not printed. It is derived from the PDF.
- **Type and format:** enum.
- **Allowed:** `yes` or `no`. `yes` in 182 rows, `no` in 9,776. Never blank.
- **Known defects:** none. 173 of the `yes` rows are in ord_PSD_110321.pdf, 8 in ord_PSD_042121.pdf (the checkbox pages) and 1 in ord_PSDNPT_040622.pdf.
- **Treat as:** a warning flag. Scan pages were read from OCR text, so most of the OCR errors and the label-first layout errors above are on scan pages.

## Corrections already applied

24 cells were corrected after the parse, each checked on the page image: 8 `recommendation` cells (the checkbox-form pages of
ord_PSD_042121.pdf, pages 149 to 156) and 16 `violations` cells (OCR errors in the cite). The tables use the corrected values.

Looked at on the page image and left as they are:

- 7 `$$1000` rows and the `$3, 500` row: printed that way on the page (the PREAMBLE rule reads them as $1,000 and $3,500).
- The two duplicate `(order_file, case_number)` pairs: two real forms (case 25064) and one identical repeated page (case 33669).
- The blank `violations` row (ord_PSD_022322.pdf page 129): the violation line is empty on the page, as are `other_party`, both dates and the city of the location.

**Answers**

- **Mean lag, 2023 orders: 227 days** (227.3 unrounded, n = 2,107)
- **Mean lag, 2024 orders: 188 days** (187.7 unrounded, n = 1,897)
- **Share of cases with lag over 365 days, all years: 12.6%** (1,259 of 9,957)

**Method**

I did not have the raw case table, so these come from the pre-computed tables in `folder-nocode/reference/tables/`:

- **Means:** table 01, section G (lags by order year), "damage->order mean" column.
- **Share over 365 days:** table 01, section G3 (lag buckets by order year). I summed the "366-730d" and ">730d" columns across all five years: 1,006 + 185 + 24 + 31 + 13 = 1,259. The bucket boundaries put 365 days in "181-365d", so the 366+ buckets match "more than 365".
- **Denominator:** the G3 buckets sum to 9,957 cases with a parseable damage date. That is one fewer than the 9,958 rows because one row has a blank damage date. 1,259 / 9,957 = 12.64%.

The figures are from the published table, not recomputed from the case rows, so they carry whatever rounding the table used.
